selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is Allah’s power compared to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is compared to the purest and brightest light.

questions.question: Which things are said to obey Allah’s command in this passage?
questions.answer: Everything, from tiny atoms to plants, animals, stars, suns, and moons.

questions.question: When many things are created, what happens to Allah’s other tasks?
questions.answer: Nothing gets mixed up, and one task does not block another.

questions.question: What example shows that a very large thing can move easily?
questions.answer: A huge ship can move as easily as a child moves a toy.

questions.question: In the army example, what can a commander send with one order?
questions.answer: He can send one soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: In the balance example, what small thing is placed on one side?
questions.answer: A walnut.

questions.question: What does Allah move as easily as atoms, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What big event in nature is compared to bringing a tree back to life?
questions.answer: Bringing the earth back to life in spring.

questions.question: What is one main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: Allah creates and gives life to many great and small things with the same ease.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use for Allah’s eternal power?
questions.answer: A very pure and shining light.

questions.question: Name three kinds of things that obey Allah in the passage.
questions.answer: Atoms, animals, and stars.

questions.question: If Allah is caring for many things, does one job delay another?
questions.answer: No, one does not interrupt another.

questions.question: What everyday example is used to help us picture easy movement?
questions.answer: A child pushing a toy.

questions.question: With the same kind of command, what two sizes of group can be sent?
questions.answer: One foot soldier or a whole army.

questions.question: In the scale example, what giant things are on the balance?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What heavenly bodies are said to move easily by Allah’s order?
questions.answer: The stars.

questions.question: What does Allah do to the earth in spring?
questions.answer: He brings it back to life like a resurrection.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what is special about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It is described as the finest and brightest light.

questions.question: Does the passage speak only about small things obeying Allah, or small and great things both?
questions.answer: It speaks about both small and great things.

questions.question: What makes it natural that many things can be created together?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is perfect, and all things submit to His command.

questions.question: For Allah’s power, are few and many treated differently?
questions.answer: No, they are the same.

questions.question: In the commander example, what remains the same when the number increases?
questions.answer: The single command.

questions.question: In the balance story, what are the two very heavy things?
questions.answer: Two mountains.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found in Allah’s power and leads to order in creation?
questions.answer: Justice and endless wisdom.
